source.title: What In-Context Learning "Learns" In-Context: Disentangling Task Recognition and Task Learning
source.authors: Jane Pan; Tianyu Gao; Howard Chen; Danqi Chen

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests task recognition and task learning in classification ICL, but does not measure induction heads, their formation, or token-index loss. It mentions induction-head studies only in related work.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work identifying induction heads, but its own experiments manipulate demonstration labels and prompts to study task recognition and abstract-label task learning. Those outcomes do not measure induction-head behavior or the specific behaviors named in V1–V7. Rows below record relevant ICL findings as none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures classification accuracy under RANDOM, ABSTRACT and GOLD label settings in GPT-3, LLaMA and OPT to separate task recognition from task learning. It does not identify, ablate or track induction heads or previous-token heads. It does not measure loss by token index or training dynamics. Induction heads appear only in related work (Olsson et al. 2022; Bansal et al. 2022). Its results therefore bear on none of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that task recognition works even in small models but does not scale. Task learning emerges in large models and improves with more demonstrations. They urge future ICL work to distinguish the two, and they note the mechanism of task learning remains unknown. They draw no conclusion about induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: No induction-head method or measure is applied; the study evaluates classification ICL by manipulating demonstration labels and prompt templates.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported task-learning trend varies with model size, number of demonstrations, abstract-label type, and task difficulty; OPT curves show significant variance.

fits_no_version.finding: RANDOM-label (task recognition) accuracy stays roughly flat across model sizes and 8–32 demonstrations. It remains above random guessing even at 350M, by about 10 points for GPT-3 ada and 5 points for OPT-350M.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task recognition in classification ICL is present in small models and does not scale with model size or number of demonstrations.

fits_no_version.finding: ABSTRACT-label (task learning) accuracy rises with model size and demonstrations. Davinci and OPT-66B match GOLD with 16 examples; LLaMA-65B does not. The rise is flatter on NLI than on sentiment tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning new input-label mappings in context emerges with scale, improves with more demonstrations, and depends on task difficulty.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2023
record.problems: The study does not measure induction heads or mechanistic contributions to ICL. Reported main trends are averages across 16 classification datasets; exact averaged values are not stated in the text. GPT-3 uses 150 examples per dataset, while OPT and LLaMA use 1,350; OPT curves have significant variance, which the authors hypothesize may reflect under-training.
record.rows_left_out: Per-dataset accuracy tables and figure-level curves are not transcribed: they concern the paper's task-recognition/task-learning construct rather than any listed induction-head version, and the text-level aggregate findings are recorded above. No values are inferred from plots.

untested.parts: No heads, composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying measured.
No training checkpoints, formation timing or loss bump measured.
No induction-head contribution and no per-token-index loss measured.
Three model families and many sizes are evaluated, but no induction behaviour is assessed in any of them.
No training data or setup is varied; only prompts, labels and demonstration counts at inference.
Few-shot task learning is measured, but it is not attributed to any heads or mechanisms, so it cannot show whether induction heads carry it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/cites_only call stands. Rows R1–R7 are correctly linked to none. The rows are text-level aggregates; per-dataset tables 4–12 are left out as declared. The task-learning results could matter for a future few-shot-mechanism claim, but no mechanism is measured, so they cannot be used for V6.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads, previous-token heads, composition, or copying behavior are measured.
No training-time formation, abruptness, loss curve, or time course of in-context learning is measured.
No induction-head contribution or loss falling with token index is measured.
Model families and sizes are varied for ICL classification performance, but induction behavior is not assessed across them or across runs, architectures, or modalities.
The paper varies prompts, labels, datasets, model sizes, and demonstration counts, but does not test induction-head formation or persistence of token-index ICL.
No heads or mechanisms are compared as carriers of few-shot learning.
No stages or sub-steps of induction-head formation are measured.

rows.subject: GPT-3 family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)
rows.operation_detail: Compared RANDOM-label ICL accuracy across model sizes and demonstration counts.

conditions.value: RANDOM (natural prompts, randomly sampled demonstration labels)

rows.baseline: Random-guess baseline shown; numerical value not stated
rows.value: RANDOM performance is described as similar across model sizes and numbers of demonstrations; with 8 examples, GPT-3 ada is around 10 points above the random baseline.
rows.uncertainty: Standard variation across three prompts is reported; magnitude not stated.
rows.note: Family-level trend and example are reported in the text; this is not an induction-head measurement.

rows.subject: LLaMA family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)
rows.operation_detail: Compared RANDOM-label ICL accuracy across model sizes and demonstration counts.

conditions.value: RANDOM (natural prompts, randomly sampled demonstration labels)

rows.baseline: Random-guess baseline shown; numerical value not stated
rows.value: RANDOM curves are described as largely flat across model sizes and demonstration counts; performance is significantly above the random baseline, including for small models and few examples.
rows.uncertainty: Standard variation across three prompts is reported; magnitude not stated.
rows.note: Family-level trend; the text gives no exact family-level accuracy values.

rows.subject: OPT family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)
rows.operation_detail: Compared RANDOM-label ICL accuracy across model sizes and demonstration counts.

conditions.value: RANDOM (natural prompts, randomly sampled demonstration labels)

rows.baseline: Random-guess baseline shown; numerical value not stated
rows.value: RANDOM performance is described as similar across model sizes and demonstration counts; even OPT-350M with 8 examples is around 5 points above the random baseline.

rows.subject: GPT-3 family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated abstract-label ICL across model sizes and demonstration counts.

conditions.value: ABSTRACT (minimal prompts and randomly mapped abstract labels)

rows.baseline: RANDOM setting is the comparison; exact value not stated
rows.value: ABSTRACT performance increases with model size and demonstration count; for davinci, with 16 examples it matches GOLD, and with the largest model and more than 16 examples ABSTRACT performs above RANDOM.
rows.uncertainty: Standard variation across three prompts is reported; magnitude not stated.
rows.note: The text states these trends but does not give exact averaged accuracy values.

rows.subject: LLaMA family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)

conditions.value: ABSTRACT (minimal prompts and randomly mapped abstract labels)

rows.baseline: RANDOM setting is the comparison; exact value not stated
rows.value: ABSTRACT performance improves with larger model size and more demonstrations, but LLaMA-65B ABSTRACT is not as competitive as its GOLD setting.
rows.uncertainty: Standard variation across three prompts is reported; magnitude not stated.
rows.note: The text reports the direction of the trend and the comparison with GOLD, without exact averaged values.

rows.subject: OPT family (family-level sweep averaged across 16 datasets)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated abstract-label ICL across model sizes and demonstration counts.

conditions.value: ABSTRACT (minimal prompts and randomly mapped abstract labels)

rows.baseline: RANDOM setting is the comparison; exact value not stated
rows.value: ABSTRACT performance improves with model size and demonstration count; OPT-66B matches GOLD with 16 examples, and ABSTRACT for the largest model with more than 16 examples performs above RANDOM.
rows.uncertainty: The paper reports significant variance in OPT curves and says variance is calculated across three prompts; magnitude not stated.

rows.subject: GPT-3 family (family-level aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared ABSTRACT performance by task type.

conditions.value: sentiment analysis versus natural language inference

rows.baseline: Sentiment analysis comparison; exact value not stated
rows.value: ABSTRACT scales better with model size and examples on sentiment analysis than on the more difficult NLI tasks; the NLI ABSTRACT curve is flatter.
rows.uncertainty: Variance across three prompts is shown in the figure; magnitude not stated.
rows.note: This task-difficulty effect concerns classification ICL, not induction behavior.
